text.p: Malta's current account deficit last year rose by two percent over 1995 to 129 million Malta pounds (about $334 million), the Central Office of Statistics said on Tuesday, quoting provisional figures.
The trade deficit for 1996 widened by 16.9 million pounds or 6.4 percent, to 281 million pounds, from 264.1 million pounds in 1995.
In the capital account, net capital flows increased by 58.3 million pounds to 72.8 million pounds in 1996.
This was the result of an increase in net inflows of 76.6 million pounds in the non-monetary sectors which arose due to a significant increase in non-resident deposits in financial institutions.
There was an increase in net outflows in the monetary sector of 18.4 million pounds from 75.4 million pounds in 1995 to 93.9 million pounds last year.
